name: Green politics
summary: Green politics seeks an ecologically sustainable society built on ecological wisdom, social justice, grassroots democracy and nonviolence. It rejects growth for its own sake, opposes nuclear power, favours decentralised participatory democracy and generous public welfare, and distrusts corporate power and free trade. Views on markets range from eco-socialist to eco-capitalist, but the mainstream backs a regulated mixed economy.
scope: The global Green party family as it states itself in the Global Greens Charter (adopted 2001, political action section updated 2012 and later), the foundational document that Britannica describes as the shared statement of Green parties worldwide. National party platforms, such as the US Green Party's, are left out as an organisation's own choices, as are green conservatism, green liberalism, green anarchism and other variants, which are separate subjects. Statements the Charter does not settle are null.
